subject: Chemistry
title: Variable n-Factor Analysis of KMnO₄, K₂Cr₂O₇, & Complex Multi-Elemental Salts
topics: KMnO₄ across 3 pH Regimes: Acidic (n=5), Neutral/Baeyer's (n=3), Basic (n=1)
Multi-Elemental Salt Oxidation: FeC₂O₄ (n=3), Fe₂(C₂O₄)₃ (n=6), Cu₂S (n=8)
Disproportionation n-Factor Formula: n_net = (n₁ · n₂) / (n₁ + n₂)
quickSummary: KMnO₄ has n=5 in acid, n=3 in neutral, n=1 in strong base. K₂Cr₂O₇ has n=6 in acid. FeC₂O₄ has n=1+2=3. Disproportionation n_net = (n₁ · n₂) / (n₁ + n₂).
summary: Master variable n-factors of KMnO₄ across pH regimes, K₂Cr₂O₇, and multi-elemental salts like FeC₂O₄.

conceptBreakdown.heading: 6.1 Potassium Permanganate (KMnO₄) Across pH Regimes
conceptBreakdown.title: 6.1 Potassium Permanganate (KMnO₄) Across pH Regimes

summaryBox.title: KMnO₄ pH Matrix
summaryBox.takeaway: Acidic: n=5 (Mn²⁺, E.M.=M/5). Neutral: n=3 (MnO₂, E.M.=M/3). Basic: n=1 (MnO₄²⁻, E.M.=M/1).

conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
KMnO₄ REDOX BEHAVIOR vs pH REGIME
                     
1. ACIDIC MEDIUM (pH < 7):
   MnO₄⁻ (+7) + 5e⁻ + 8H⁺ → Mn²⁺ (+2) + 4H₂O
   n-factor = |+7 - (+2)| = 5  ⟹  E.M. = M/5 = 158.04/5 = 31.61 g/eq
      
2. NEUTRAL / FAINTLY ALKALINE MEDIUM (pH = 7–9, Baeyer's Reagent):
   MnO₄⁻ (+7) + 3e⁻ + 2H₂O → MnO₂ (+4) + 4OH⁻
   n-factor = |+7 - (+4)| = 3  ⟹  E.M. = M/3 = 158.04/3 = 52.68 g/eq
      
3. STRONGLY BASIC MEDIUM (pH > 12):
   MnO₄⁻ (+7) + e⁻ → MnO₄²⁻ (+6) (Manganate Ion)
   n-factor = |+7 - (+6)| = 1  ⟹  E.M. = M/1 = 158.04 g/eq
conceptBreakdown.content:
Potassium Permanganate is an exceptional oxidizing agent whose reduction product is governed by solution pH:

1. **Acidic Medium ($\text{pH} < 7$)**: $\text{MnO}_4^- (+7) \rightarrow \text{Mn}^{2+} (+2) \implies \mathbf{n = 5}, \mathbf{\text{E.M.} = M/5 = 31.61\text{ g/eq}}$.
2. **Neutral / Faintly Basic ($\text{pH} = 7\text{--}9$, Baeyer's Reagent)**: $\text{MnO}_4^- (+7) \rightarrow \text{MnO}_2 (+4) \implies \mathbf{n = 3}, \mathbf{\text{E.M.} = M/3 = 52.68\text{ g/eq}}$.
3. **Strongly Basic Medium ($\text{pH} > 12$)**: $\text{MnO}_4^- (+7) \rightarrow \text{MnO}_4^{2-} (+6) \implies \mathbf{n = 1}, \mathbf{\text{E.M.} = M/1 = 158.04\text{ g/eq}}$.

conceptBreakdown.heading: 6.2 K₂Cr₂O₇ and Complex Poly-Elemental Salts
conceptBreakdown.title: 6.2 K₂Cr₂O₇ and Complex Poly-Elemental Salts
conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
n-FACTOR FOR MULTI-ELEMENTAL OXIDATION

• K₂Cr₂O₇ (in acid): Cr₂O₇²⁻ (+6) → 2 Cr³⁺ (+3)
  n = 2 atoms × |6 - 3| = 6  ⟹  E.M. = M/6 = 49.03 g/eq

• Ferrous Oxalate (FeC₂O₄ → Fe³⁺ + 2 CO₂):
  Fe²⁺ → Fe³⁺ (n₁ = 1)  PLUS  C₂O₄²⁻ → 2 CO₂ (n₂ = 2)
  n_net = 1 + 2 = 3  ⟹  E.M. = M/3

• Disproportionation: n_net = (n₁ · n₂) / (n₁ + n₂)
conceptBreakdown.content:
• **Potassium Dichromate ($\text{K}_2\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7$)**: Acts as an oxidant strictly in acidic medium:
  $$\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7^{2-} (+6) + 14\text{H}^+ + 6e^- \rightarrow 2\text{Cr}^{3+} (+3) + 7\text{H}_2\text{O} \implies \mathbf{n = 6}, \mathbf{\text{E.M.} = M/6 = 49.03\text{ g/eq}}$$
• **Multi-Elemental Salt Oxidation (Ferrous Oxalate, $\text{FeC}_2\text{O}_4$)**:
  - $\text{Fe}^{2+} \rightarrow \text{Fe}^{3+} + e^- \implies n_1 = 1$
  - $\text{C}_2\text{O}_4^{2-} \rightarrow 2\text{CO}_2 + 2e^- \implies n_2 = 2$
  - Net $n = n_1 + n_2 = 1 + 2 = \mathbf{3} \implies \mathbf{\text{E.M.} = M/3}$.
• **Disproportionation Formula**: For a single reactant undergoing both oxidation ($n_{\text{ox}}$) and reduction ($n_{\text{red}}$):
  $$\mathbf{n_{\text{net}} = \frac{n_{\text{ox}} \cdot n_{\text{red}}}{n_{\text{ox}} + n_{\text{red}}}}$$

quickRevision: KMnO₄: n=5 (acid), n=3 (neutral/faint base), n=1 (strong base).
K₂Cr₂O₇ in acid has n=6 (E.M. = M/6).
FeC₂O₄ oxidized to Fe³⁺ and CO₂ has n-factor = 3.
